raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20260921T213616413545-router-wire (node router-wire), plan imas-ambix:serve-telemetry-spine section 6. Basis: commits abd3128f (test) and d7f02c4b (docs) over base 489ea67b, four paths, +383 lines, zero production lines; range unmerged to origin/main at review time; worktree clean.

WHAT THE CHANGE IS. Section 6 asks that the request stream follow from the launch. The production path is cli.py:1660 (lane_document=_Path(site.endpoint_document).with_name("lane.json")), from which RouterApp derives requests.jsonl beside the lane document (router.py:236-241). The reviewed commit adds tests/test_agent_router_telemetry.py (178 lines, new), mounting three assertions on the launch construction itself (RouterApp built with lane_document only): a relayed request lands a row beside the lane document with model/upstream/status/token fields; a caller that departs before the body is read leaves one aborted row with upstream "(router)"; an explicit receipts path still wins and no derived file appears. It reuses the existing harness (tests/test_agent_router.py, tests/test_request_receipts.py) rather than building a second driver. The docs commit records claim, measure and result in the plan's archive anchor, adds a figure embedded with a project-absolute src, and adds 3 lines to the live plan.

REPRODUCTION (mine, in a scratch copy of the revised tree, run from a neutral CWD). Baseline over the new file plus the three pre-existing modules: 30 passed, exit 0. The node's own wider gate re-run: 37 passed, exit 0, matching its gate log.

NEGATIVE CONTROL - WHAT WAS DECLARED, WHAT WAS RUN, AND WHICH IS BETTER AIMED. The coordinator declared "delete the call that records the request receipt on the relay response path". The node instead mutated the derivation `self._receipts_path = lane_document.with_name(RECEIPTS_FILENAME)` -> `self._receipts_path = None` and reported 2 failed / 1 passed.

I ran both, independently. Mutation A (derivation -> None), all four files: 2 failed / 28 passed, the failures being exactly the two named new assertions, with the third (explicit path) still green, separating derivation from precedence. Mutation A with the new file absent: 27 passed / 0 failed, so the derivation was held by nothing before this node and the gap is visible as a positive control. Mutation B (delete the relay-path self._record_receipt(...) call, as declared): 8 failed / 22 passed, of which six failures are pre-existing tests in tests/test_request_receipts.py (test_every_relayed_request_writes_one_fully_populated_row, test_aborted_request_is_recorded_as_aborted_rather_than_dropped, test_upstream_error_is_recorded_as_failed, test_an_unwritable_destination_cannot_disturb_the_relay, test_an_upstream_that_dies_mid_body_is_recorded_as_failed, test_the_sampling_ceiling_is_read_from_the_environment) plus two of the new ones; the departure assertion stays green under B because that path records through _record_self_answer, a different call site.

Verdict: the substitution is BETTER AIMED than what was declared, and not a way of avoiding a harder control. The declared control is already held by six pre-existing tests, so it cannot demonstrate the thing the node was dispatched to close; a node reporting it would have shown a red that says nothing about this change's gap. The node's mutation reddens exactly the new assertion set and, run against the pre-existing files alone, shows zero failures - the unheld derivation made visible. Both are the same kind of one-line edit, so B is not harder to perform than A; "avoiding the harder one" is not supported by the evidence.

WORTH PROMOTING ON ITS OWN TERMS? Yes - as a verification/guard node. The section's wiring had already landed before dispatch: 0e9a656c (feat) and 9467fc0d (fix) are ancestors of the base, and the relevant modules are byte-identical between the base and the reviewer's HEAD. The worker contract covers exactly this case (verify behaviour that is already correct and add the missing test rather than reimplementing a working guard), and the node did that: zero production lines, a focused assertion set mounted on the production construction, and a control that establishes the prior absence. The dispatch is better read as "make the section's done-when measurable" than as an implementation slot; the plan's sequencing note implying the wiring was still to come is stale and should be corrected. What is genuinely still unwired - the recorder tick's supply to a stored row in serving_receipts.py - belongs to recorder-wire, not here.

EDGE NOTE, NOT A DEFECT. tests/test_agent_router_telemetry.py:128 compares against SELF_ANSWERED_UPSTREAM imported from the module under test; the literal pin lives in tests/test_request_receipts.py:679. The pending circular-assertion-guard plan already classifies "a value pinned once and referenced thereafter" as a sound shape requiring an allowlist entry, so this is an entry to scope rather than a fault; recorded as a low-severity finding for that guard's coverage.

VERIFIED, INDEPENDENTLY. Production call site cli.py:1660 present and true; diff base->d7f02c4b touches only the four declared paths (+383, zero production lines); plan meta lines untouched; figure embedded with project-absolute src at the archive anchor; commits carry conventional subjects with bodies and no attribution trailers; the node did not close its own node.
